body:
Macquarie PE, the private equity arm of Australia-based global asset manager Macquarie Asset Management, has signed a definitive agreement to acquire South Korean cosmetics manufacturers Hwasung Cosmetics and Nowcos for approximately ₩300 billion (approximately $216.6 million). The deal was finalized just one month after Macquarie PE was selected as the preferred bidder, illustrating how global private equity investment in K-beauty is expanding from brands into manufacturing infrastructure.

According to investment banking industry sources, Macquarie PE signed the share purchase agreement (SPA) with private equity firm Affirma Capital on the 18th. The transaction covers Affirma Capital's 70% stake in Hwasung Cosmetics and its 100% stake in Nowcos. Macquarie PE also plans to acquire the remaining 30% stake held by Hwasung Cosmetics founder Ryu Kyung-hoon and other shareholders at a later date.

Samsung Securities and Rothschild served as sell-side advisors. With this transaction, Affirma Capital has recovered its investment seven years after acquiring management control of Hwasung Cosmetics in 2019.

The sale process for Hwasung Cosmetics began in March of this year. Five to six parties participated in the preliminary bidding round, and in the final round, Macquarie PE competed against a consortium of Korea Investment Private Equity and EcoPro Partners, as well as a European strategic investor.

Affirma Capital has maintained a steady record of investment recoveries this year, having completed the sale of Sungkyung Food and Seah E&S before closing this transaction. The firm is currently in the process of raising its seventh blind-pool fund with a target size of ₩500 billion (approximately $361.0 million).

The two companies each hold differentiated competitive positions in the color cosmetics and skincare segments, respectively. Hwasung Cosmetics is an original design manufacturer (ODM) producing color cosmetics such as eyebrow products, supplying global major brands including L'Oréal and Estée Lauder as well as South Korean indie brands. Nowcos is an ODM specializing in skincare products.

Affirma Capital enhanced the corporate value of both companies through a bolt-on strategy of acquiring peer companies in the same industry. After acquiring a 70% founder stake in Hwasung Cosmetics in 2019 to secure management control, the firm purchased Nowcos in 2022 and strengthened R&D investment and marketing targeting overseas customers.

Hwasung Cosmetics' revenue grew approximately 2.2-fold from ₩50.1 billion (approximately $36.2 million) in 2019 to ₩110.6 billion (approximately $79.8 million) last year. Over the same period, operating profit increased approximately 5.2-fold from ₩3.8 billion (approximately $2.7 million) to ₩19.8 billion (approximately $14.3 million). Last year's EBITDA was approximately ₩24 billion (approximately $17.3 million). Nowcos generated revenue of approximately ₩69.5 billion (approximately $50.2 million) last year.

In February of this year, Affirma Capital conducted a tender offer for the remaining shares of Nowcos, which was listed on the KONEX market, and voluntarily delisted the company. The move was seen as a measure to remove the burden of maintaining a listing and increase the likelihood of a successful sale to a potential acquirer.

This transaction aligns with a broader trend of global private equity investment in K-beauty expanding from brand-focused deals to manufacturing and distribution infrastructure across the board.

KKR acquired cosmetics container manufacturer Samhwa last year for ₩730 billion (approximately $527.0 million). CVC Capital invested ₩300 billion (approximately $216.6 million) in K-beauty distribution company Silicon2 in August of this year. Macquarie PE's latest acquisition is interpreted as a move in the same vein—securing foundational assets in the K-beauty industry.

Macquarie Asset Management is a global asset manager headquartered in Australia with strengths in infrastructure investment. In South Korea, it has invested in DIG Airgas, LG CNS, S&I Corporation, and Genuone Sciences. The firm has recently recovered substantial investment capital, securing capacity for new investments.

Earlier this year, Macquarie sold industrial gas company DIG Airgas to France's Air Liquide for approximately ₩4.85 trillion (approximately $3.5 billion), and disposed of its entire remaining stake in LG CNS through a block deal, recovering ₩530 billion (approximately $382.6 million).
